questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on a surface with good grip, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on a surface with good grip, keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle will stay under control if it is upright and moving straight.

questions.question: The body removes about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To estimate drinks remaining in the system, subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. In this case, eight drinks minus four hours equals about four drinks remaining.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees they will yield to you.
Is not worth the effort.
Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
Means the driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with another driver means they will properly yield to you. Always be ready to take action.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns solid yellow, you should:

options.text: Get ready to stop.
Speed up.
Put the vehicle in reverse and back up.
Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means the light will turn red soon. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you can safely stop before entering the intersection, do so.

questions.question: To stop as quickly as possible, you should:

options.text: Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes together.
questions.explanation: For the quickest stop, use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light when:

options.text: You see a police officer.
Another vehicle is tailgating you.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your turn signals are broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: Another vehicle is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light if a vehicle is following too closely. This warns the driver that you are about to slow down. This is especially helpful when slowing in unexpected places.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How fast the alcohol was consumed
How often a person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount consumed, how quickly it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and whether they have eaten also matter. How often someone drinks does not affect their current BAC.

questions.question: An integrated braking system:

options.text: Applies some rear braking when you use the front brake.
Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake.
Applies equal braking to both front and rear when either is used.
Remembers how hard you usually brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies some front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Check your owner's manual for details about your specific motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: A major effect of alcohol is:

options.text: Better riding skills.
Slowing down body and mind.
More nervousness.
Better alertness.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down body and mind.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down and weakens both your physical and mental abilities.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks, you should:

options.text: Keep holding the brake and the skid will stop.
Release the front brake and avoid using it again.
Release the front brake, then squeeze it again quickly.
Release the front brake right away and then apply it smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and then apply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake completely and immediately. Then apply the brake smoothly to regain control.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: Never.
Only during the day.
Only at night.
Day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials makes you more visible at all times.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop completely, then go if it is safe.
Go slowly through the intersection. You may not need to stop.
Stop only if there is traffic on the crossing road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go if it is safe.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must make a complete stop. Only go when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Kick it away.
Stop until it loses interest.
Swerve around it.
Approach it slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. Slow down and approach the dog calmly. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: Why should you keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You can pass dangers more quickly.
You have a narrow view so you can focus better.
You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
You can more easily follow the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles gives you a better view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to move around them.

questions.question: What color are work area signs?

options.text: Orange with black letters or symbols.
White with red letters or symbols.
Blue with white letters or symbols.
Green with white letters or symbols.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange with black letters or symbols.
questions.explanation: Work area signs are orange with black letters and symbols. Slow down in work areas and follow all signs, signals, and directions from workers.

questions.question: Riding clothes should protect you from all of the following, except:

options.text: Sunburn.
Windburn.
Chapped lips.
Dehydration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips.
questions.explanation: Riding clothes protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, cold, dehydration, and the motorcycle itself. They also protect you in a crash.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift to neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like schools and construction zones, position your hands on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: The center of a traffic lane often has an oily strip. Is it safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: Never safe.
Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe in all weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles. The strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can often ride around it and stay in the center lane.

questions.question: What does it mean if you make eye contact with another driver?

options.text: The best way to know they see you.
Not worth the effort.
It does not mean they will give way to you.
They will always give way to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will give way to you.
questions.explanation: Eye contact is not a guarantee that a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look right at motorcyclists but don't see them.

questions.question: How should you brake on a slippery surface?

options.text: Use both front and rear brakes.
Press hard on the front brake to prevent the front tire from locking.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the front brake lever slowly and use gentle pressure on the rear brake to avoid locking the wheels.
